newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Mixed trading seen in FTSE, BAT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Mixed trading seen in FTSE, BAT.

text.p: A lively session in UK equity options on Thursday was spearheaded by frantic trading in FTSE 100 index contracts ahead of Friday's expiry, dealers said.

One trader sold 1,000 June 4625 puts and calls at about 14-1/2p and 12p each in a short straddle strategy. If this was an opening deal, it would require June futures to fall to 4625 by 0930 GMT tomorrow -- when index futures and options expire -- to make a maximum profit of 26-1/2p.
There were also several buyers of put options in FTSE who were betting the market would plunge. A couple of traders bought 500 June 4575 puts at 3p.
Another deal was to buy 500 June 4600 puts at 6p.
By 1420 GMT, cash FTSE was down 6.7 at 4650.3 while June FTSE futures were down 8.0 at 4644.0.
Also busy were options in B.A.T. Industries as hopes were raised that a settlement would soon be announced regarding tobacco related lawsuits .

One of the larger deals was to buy 500 July 550 calls at 37p. Another was a crossed trade in which 250 October 550 puts were traded at 28p along with 250 October 600 calls at 33p in a strangle strategy.
Elsewhere, there was a buyer of 1,700 July 120 calls at 4p in supermarket chain Asda Group.
And in recently floated insurer Norwich Union a split synthetic long position was created in the belief the shares will go higher.

The strategy involved buying 750 September 330 calls at 20p and selling 750 September 300 puts at 10p for a net debit of 10p. At expiry, the deal will make a profit if the shares climb above 340p. Norwich Union shares gained 5-1/2p to 324p and those of Asda shed 1/2p to 120-3/4p.
-- Pradip Mishra, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5113 *FOR FUTURES AND OPTIONS EXPIRY DATES PLEASE SEE PAGE UKA4 *
